transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2026-05-08
Time: 14:00 UTC
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Carlos Mendez (Redwood SE note), Aisha Khan (ZenOptic Product), Tom Rivers (ZenOptic Head of ML), Maya Patel (ZenOptic Security), Evan Cho (ZenOptic Platform)

Summary (auto):
Quick model catalog walkthrough focusing on how to choose open models, interpret Redwood benchmark profiles, and read compatibility matrices for dedicated vs hosted deployments. Discussed latency vs cost tradeoffs, quantization and KV-cache compatibility, and next steps for micro-benchmarks and procurement.

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone thanks for joining, we really appreciate you carving out time. I think the agenda is a quick run through the model catalog in the Console, how the benchmarks are reported, then compatibility matrices and suggested picks for ZenOptic workloads — and leave time for Q&A.
[00:17] Aisha: Sounds good, Jordan. For context, we're trying to pick an open model to replace our current Llama2 instance for clinical triage summarization, so latency and hallucination rates are both very important.
[00:30] Tom: Yeah and cost — we run thousands of short prompts per hour so per-token cost and batching behaviour matter.
[00:37] Priya: Great, we'll surface the profiles that match that pattern. Quick question: are you planning Dedicated or hosted to start? I know procurement is involved.
[00:46] Evan: Ideally hosted to start for speed to market but we need to evaluate VPC/private options later for PHI.
[00:54] Maya: And on compliance — SOC 2, SSO/SAML, and key management are musts. We'll want audit logs and KMS integration.
[01:03] Jordan: Absolutely, we have Private deployment options and KMS/HSM integrations; we'll attach the security pack after. But today, model selection. Priya, can you share your screen?
[01:12] Priya: Yep — pulling up the Redwood Console model catalog now. I'm on the model list view. You'll notice models are grouped by family, license, and recommended use cases. There's a quick filter: conversational, summarization, embeddings, and a "short prompts / high qps" tag.
[01:33] Priya: For ZenOptic's short clinical triage prompts, I generally recommend starting with the 7B and 13B open variants that we have benchmarked — the 13B quantized profile tends to hit a good latency sweet spot with low regression in quality.
[01:48] Tom: When you say quantized profile — do you mean 4-bit Q4 or an 8-bit option?
[01:52] Priya: We publish both Q4 and Q8 profiles. The model catalog shows per-model performance for each quantization profile and hardware class — e.g., A10G vs H100 vs CPU. The compatibility matrix indicates which kernels and KV-cache behaviors are supported for each quant config.
[02:10] Carlos: One gotcha to watch: some third-party quantized weights don't support persistent KV cache well, so beam-search long-context flows can regress. We flag those in the matrix under "KV cache compatibility" with a little red/amber/green.
[02:25] Aisha: Is there an easy way to compare latency and cost across models in the UI?
[02:29] Priya: Yes, on each model card we have a benchmark summary: p50/p95 latency for short prompts, tokens/sec throughput, and an estimated $/K token cost assuming default batching heuristics. You can toggle region and instance type to see changes.
[02:43] Tom: Do those benchmarks run on your standard prompt suite? I'm concerned our clinical language might shift latency because of tokenization differences.
[02:51] Priya: Good point. We run a standardized benchmark, but you can upload a small representative prompt set and run a private micro-benchmark in the console. That's what we recommend — we'll run that for you as an SE follow-up.
[03:03] Jordan: I'll add that to action items — Priya will run the micro-benchmark with the sample prompts.
[03:07] Maya: On the compatibility matrix — can you show the security column? I want to see encryption at rest, logs, and access controls.
[03:14] Priya: Sure — the matrix has flag for "Private deployment support" and separate fields for "KMS/HSM supported", "Audit logs available", and "SAML/SSO integration tested". For hosted models we surface data-retention choices and for Dedicated/Private we show the additional controls.
[03:31] Evan: If we choose Dedicated, how does model pinning and rollouts work? We have a canary flow in our infra.
[03:38] Priya: We support model version pinning per route, canary rollouts, traffic-splitting, and automatic fallback to a compatible variant if the primary model OOMs or is unavailable. The compatibility matrix includes which runtime variants are cross-compatible for fallback.
[03:51] Tom: Any customers using your 13B quantized on A10G for low-latency short prompts in prod?
[03:57] Priya: Yes — several. In the catalog we link to verified performance profiles and anonymized benchmarks. We also show community notes; caveat: anonymized customer datasets might differ.
[04:08] Aisha: About hallucination — do you provide evals or metrics per model on truthfulness for summarization tasks?
[04:15] Priya: We have per-model eval buckets. For summarization we show ROUGE/L and an internal factuality score run on our eval set; again you can run your own evals with your reference data via Redwood Optimize.
[04:27] Jordan: I'm going to demo the compatibility matrix view now — you'll see columns for license (e.g., Apache2, L4), quantization profiles, hardware compat, tokenization caveats, KV cache support, and runtime flags.
[04:43] [04:43] Jordan (cont): There's also an export button to get a CSV you can share with procurement.
[04:48] Tom: Great. Can you show an example of how the estimated $/K tokens is computed?
[04:54] Priya: The estimate is based on the observed tokens-per-second in our benchmarks, instance pricing for the selected region, and typical batching heuristics. It's conservative. For example, a 13B Q4 on A10G in us-east gives about X ms p95 and an estimated $Y per 1K prompt tokens.
[05:14] Maya: We need to validate that the instance pricing aligns with our cloud provider contracts — do you publish the assumptions used?
[05:20] Jordan: Yes, the spreadsheet we'll share includes the assumptions and the kernel/hardware mapping.
[05:26] Evan: About KV cache — our flow keeps context ~2k tokens and reuses a lot of prefixes. How does that affect throughput?
[05:33] Priya: Prefix/KV cache helps a lot for repeated prefixes. The catalog profile includes a "prefix reuse" throughput boost estimate. If you have high prefix reuse, effective tokens/sec increases substantially and cost drops. We'll measure that in the micro-benchmark.
[05:46] Tom: Any limitations around function calling or structured output with these open models?
[05:52] Priya: Functional calling is supported at the API layer for all compatible models, but some quantized runtime stacks require additional shaping for structured tool-calls; it's listed in the matrix as "function-call verified".
[06:06] Aisha: Can you walk through a concrete recommendation for our use-case — short clinical triage prompts, 2k context, need low hallucination, start hosted then maybe Dedicated?
[06:16] Priya: Recommendation: start with the 13B Q4 open variant on hosted. It balances latency and quality for short prompts and supports KV cache. If you need stricter isolation, move to Dedicated with the same model family; the matrix shows matching runtime variants. Also run a factuality eval via Redwood Optimize.
[06:33] Tom: If we move to Dedicated, how do upgrades/rollouts happen? Will we have downtime?
[06:38] Carlos: Rollouts are canary-based and support zero-downtime in most cases thanks to the runtime's session pinning and fallback. We also support scheduled maintenance windows.
[06:49] Maya: For the security docs, is there a SOC2 report and pen-test summary we can review?
[06:54] Jordan: Yes — I'll attach SOC2 and ISO certs and a high-level pen test summary. We'll also provide a data flow diagram for PHI handling.
[07:03] [07:03] Tom (interruption): Sorry real quick — about tokenizer differences you mentioned earlier, how often do you see tokenization causing 10-20% latency differences?
[07:12] Priya: It's workload-dependent. Clinical shorthand can compress or expand tokens; that's why we recommend running your prompt set in a micro-benchmark. In some corner cases, tokenization can change cost estimates by 15%.
[07:25] Aisha: Any advice on prompt engineering to reduce hallucination without increasing latency?
[07:31] Priya: Temperature tuning, scaffolded prompts and context windows help. Also we recommend system-level instructions and few-shot examples in the prompt — those are cheap token-wise if you leverage KV cache for repeated system prompts.
[07:45] Evan: About the model catalog UI — is there an API to fetch the compatibility matrix so we can automate checks during CI?
[07:52] Priya: Yes, there's a model-catalog API endpoint that returns JSON. We'll provide the API key scope info; in Private/Dedicated you can host a synced copy internally.
[08:03] Tom: Are there any license landmines for the open models you surface? We need to avoid copyleft for production.
[08:10] Priya: We flag license types prominently. Some community variants have more restrictive terms; the catalog shows license tags and a short human-readable summary. Procurement should review, and we can escalate legal if needed.
[08:22] Aisha: Example: if a model is L4 or Apache-2, how do we interpret that in terms of usage?
[08:28] Jordan: L4 generally indicates limited commercial use; Apache-2 is permissive. We'll include a short license guide in the deck we send.
[08:36] Maya: On audit logs and retention, can we configure retention windows per route?
[08:41] Priya: For enterprise plans you can set retention windows and log-forwarding to your SIEM. In Dedicated/Private you control retention via your infra.
[08:50] Carlos: Quick note — if you plan deterministic outputs, we have deterministic seeding and a "strict inference" mode that reduces nondeterminism at the cost of throughput. It's in the matrix under "determinism support".
[09:01] Aisha: That's interesting, might be helpful for high-assurance summarization.
[09:05] [09:05] Jordan: We're about to wrap — any other major blockers?
[09:09] Tom: Procurement will want ballpark numbers for a pilot and Dedicated pricing.
[09:13] Jordan: We'll provide pilot pricing options and a Dedicated SKU example.
[09:17] Maya: We'll send over compliance doc list by Monday.
[09:20] Jordan: Great. Recap and next steps: Jordan to send model catalog playbook, benchmark spreadsheet, security docs; Priya to run micro-benchmark; schedule pricing call.
[09:29] Aisha: Thanks everyone, that was helpful.
[09:32] Jordan: Thanks all, we'll follow up with the links.
[09:36] End of recording.
